# MCP

A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) endpoint at `/mcp`, so an agent (Claude Code, a Claude
connector, any Streamable HTTP client) can manage your app and call its own tools. No sidecar process.

- Built-in `pb_*` tools for collections, records, settings, logs and backups.
- Your `pb_hooks` add tools with `$mcp.addTool`, and other plugins add them from Go.
- Sign-in with OAuth through [OAuth Server](/docs/plugins/oauth-server): add `https://<host>/mcp` to Claude and sign in
  in a browser.

A Go port of [pbjsmcp](https://github.com/benallfree/pbjsmcp), with the same tool names and safety rules.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations)

## Install

MCP is built into `pocketone` and always on, with [Tokens](/docs/plugins/tokens) and
[OAuth Server](/docs/plugins/oauth-server) for sign-in and `$mcp` in `pb_hooks`. There's nothing to install or turn on.

In your own Go build, register it before the app starts. Register Tokens and OAuth Server too for OAuth sign-in, and
bind `$mcp` into the JS hooks if you use them:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
tokens.MustRegister(app, tokens.Config{})
oauthserver.MustRegister(app, oauthserver.Config{})
mcp.MustRegister(app, mcp.Config{})
jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{OnInit: func(vm *goja.Runtime) { mcp.BindJS(vm, app) }})
app.Start()
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/mcp`.

## Configure

In `pocketone` there is no `pocketone.yaml` section, flag or environment variable for MCP. It serves `/mcp` with every
built-in tool, and only superusers can sign in.

### Scopes

When a client signs in, it asks for one or both MCP scopes, and you approve them on the consent page:

| Scope | Allows |
|---|---|
| `mcp:read` | Seeing and calling only the tools marked read-only. |
| `mcp:write` | Every tool you're allowed to use, including ones that change data. Includes `mcp:read`. |

A client that asks only for `offline_access` gets the account's full rights, still limited to `/mcp`. Calling a tool
the grant doesn't cover gets `403` with `error="insufficient_scope", scope="mcp:write"`, so the client can ask for
more.

### Behind a proxy

The OAuth resource URL must match the URL clients use. MCP builds it from the request's host, taking the scheme from
`X-Forwarded-Proto` or from **Settings → Application URL** when its host is the same. If your proxy rewrites the host,
set `Config.PublicURL` in a Go build.

## Use

### Connect Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http my-app https://<host>/mcp
claude mcp login my-app        # or /mcp in a session
```

A browser opens on your app's sign-in page. Sign in as a superuser, check the scopes and click **Allow**.

For a Claude connector, paste `https://<host>/mcp` into Claude's **Add custom connector** and sign in the same way.

### See and revoke connected clients

Each sign-in creates an API token bound to `/mcp`. They're listed under **Settings → API tokens** with an
`oauth: <client>` label; click **Revoke** to disconnect a client.

### Built-in tools

They call the app directly, so they bypass collection API rules. Every one requires a superuser.

| Group | Tools |
|---|---|
| `info` | `pb_server_info` |
| `collections` | `pb_list_collections`, `pb_get_collection`, `pb_create_collection`, `pb_update_collection`, `pb_delete_collection`, `pb_import_collections` |
| `records` | `pb_list_records`, `pb_get_record`, `pb_create_record`, `pb_update_record`, `pb_delete_record` |
| `settings` | `pb_get_settings`, `pb_update_settings` |
| `logs` | `pb_list_logs` |
| `backups` | `pb_list_backups`, `pb_create_backup` |

Safety:

- `pb_delete_collection` needs `confirm` set to the collection name.
- Imports never delete collections.
- Records come back without hidden fields.
- Settings come back without SMTP and S3 secrets.
- Restoring backups and uploading files are not exposed.

### Add your own tools from pb_hooks

```js
// pb_hooks/mcp.pb.js, at the top level
$mcp.addTool({
  name: 'count_posts',
  description: 'Count published posts.',
  annotations: { readOnlyHint: true },
  allow: 'superuser', // default; "auth" = any signed-in record; ["users"] = those collections
  handler: ({ args, auth, app, e }) => ({ count: app.countRecords('posts', $dbx.hashExp({ published: true })) }),
})
$mcp.instructions('count_posts counts only published posts.')
```

- Call `$mcp.addTool` only at the top level of a hooks file. `inputSchema`, `outputSchema` and `title` are optional.
- Unlike `routerAdd` handlers, tool handlers can use the file's top-level variables. They run one at a time on the VM
  that loaded the hooks, so keep them short.
- Throw to return a tool error the model can read.
- Only tools with `readOnlyHint: true` are available to an `mcp:read` grant.
- `$mcp.tools()` lists the registered tool names.

In `pocketone` only superusers can sign in to `/mcp`, so `allow: 'auth'` still means superusers there.

### In the logs

Without OAuth Server on the app, MCP logs a warning on serve: `mcp: ext/oauth-server isn't registered`. In `pocketone`
it always is.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Plugin | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [OAuth Server](/docs/plugins/oauth-server) | Signs MCP clients in. MCP turns on its client self-registration, and points clients at it from the protected resource metadata. Who may sign in comes from its `Collections` (default: superusers). |
| [Tokens](/docs/plugins/tokens) | MCP registers `mcp:read` and `mcp:write` as token scopes. The access tokens are API tokens bound to `https://<host>/mcp` (RFC 8707): Tokens refuses them anywhere else, and `/mcp` accepts only tokens bound to itself. |
| JS hooks | `$mcp` in `pb_hooks` (above). |

### Sign-in flow

With Tokens and OAuth Server on the app, `/mcp` uses OAuth the way Claude connectors and Claude Code expect:

1. A request without a token gets `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://<host>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp", scope="mcp:read mcp:write"`.
2. The protected resource metadata names the app as its authorization server. OAuth Server publishes the authorization
   server metadata, with PKCE S256, client metadata documents and dynamic registration.
3. The client registers itself, either with Claude's published identity (a client metadata document from `claude.ai`
   or `claude.com`) or with dynamic registration. The user signs in in a browser and approves the scopes.
4. The access token is an API token bound to `https://<host>/mcp`. Deploy tokens and pasted PocketBase tokens are
   refused, unless you set `mcp.OAuth{AllowUnbound: true}`.

The authorization server listed in the metadata is OAuth Server's issuer (its `Config.Issuer`, else the request's
scheme and host). `OAuth.Issuer` overrides it.

Without OAuth Server, `/mcp` falls back to `PocketBaseTokenAuth`: pasted superuser PocketBase tokens with full scope,
and the warning above. The authenticator is chosen on serve, so plugin registration order doesn't matter.
`Config.Auth` overrides the choice.

### Adding tools from Go

Another plugin on the same app reaches the server with `mcp.For(app)`:

```go
mcp.For(app).MustAddTool(mcp.Tool{
    Name:        "count_posts",
    Description: "Count published posts.",
    Annotations: mcp.Read,
    Handler: func(c *mcp.Call) (any, error) {
        n, err := c.App.CountRecords("posts", dbx.HashExp{"published": true})
        return map[string]any{"count": n}, err
    },
})
```

The full tool definition:

```go
mcp.Tool{
    Name:         "tool_name",           // 1-128 of A-Za-z0-9_.-, unique per app
    Title:        "Tool name",
    Description:  "What it does, for the model.",
    InputSchema:  map[string]any{...},    // JSON Schema; default: no arguments
    OutputSchema: map[string]any{...},    // optional
    Annotations:  mcp.Read,               // or mcp.Write, mcp.Destroy, or your own
    Allow:        mcp.RequireSuperuser,   // default; mcp.RequireAuth("users"), or any func(*mcp.Call) error
    Handler:      func(c *mcp.Call) (any, error) { ... },
}
```

- `c.Args` holds the arguments. `c.Auth()` is the signed-in record, `c.Grant` holds its scopes and client, and `c.App`
  and `c.Event` are the app and the request.
- Return any JSON-able value. It's sent as text, and also as `structuredContent` when it's an object.
- Return an error (or panic) to report a tool failure (`isError: true`) that the model can read.
- `Allow` decides who sees the tool at all. A caller it rejects gets "Unknown tool", the same as for a tool that
  doesn't exist.
- Arguments are not validated against `InputSchema`, so check the ones you rely on.
- `AddInstructions(text)` adds a paragraph to the `instructions` sent in `initialize`. `RemoveTool(name)` and
  `Tools()` round out the API.

## Go config

| Field | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `Path` | `/mcp` | Endpoint path. |
| `Name`, `Version`, `Description`, `Icons` | app name slug, `dev` | `serverInfo` (its title is Settings → Application name). |
| `Instructions` | generated | First paragraph of `instructions`. |
| `PublicURL` | the request's scheme and host | Origin used for the OAuth resource URL. Set it when a proxy rewrites the host. |
| `Auth` | `OAuth{}` with OAuth Server and Tokens, else `PocketBaseTokenAuth{}` | The `Authenticator`. |
| `BuiltinGroups` | all | Built-in tool groups to register (`info`, `collections`, `records`, `settings`, `logs`, `backups`). |
| `ReadOnlyBuiltins` | `false` | Keep only the read-only built-in tools. |
| `NoBuiltins` | `false` | Leave out every built-in tool. |
| `AllowedOrigins` | none | Extra browser origins. Requests with any other `Origin` header get 403. Clients that send no `Origin`, such as Claude's servers and Claude Code, pass. |

## How it works

- MCP Streamable HTTP, stateless: each POST carries one JSON-RPC message and gets JSON back. `GET` and `DELETE` get
  405; batches are refused. Protocol versions `2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18` and `2025-03-26`. Tools only for now.
- The protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) is served at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and
  `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`.
- Request bodies are limited to 4 MiB.

## Example

```bash
cd example
go build -o pbmcp .
./pbmcp superuser upsert test@example.com testpassword123 --dir=pb_data
./pbmcp serve --dir=pb_data
```

The example registers [devusers](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/devusers/devusers.go), so the logins are `admin@example.com` / `password`
(superuser) and `user@example.com` / `password` (user). It also registers Tokens and OAuth Server for OAuth sign-in,
and adds a Go tool (`whoami`, for any signed-in record) and a JS tool (`recent_users`, in `pb_hooks/mcp.pb.js`). Then:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http pb-example http://127.0.0.1:8090/mcp
claude mcp login pb-example
```
